title: Gradual latency spiral: capture & mitigation (SRE draft)
content:
Summary:

We observed a slow, persistent latency increase across one Dedicated GPU pool over ~36 hours that then produced recurring short bursts of 95th-percentile latency spikes. This doc captures detection signals, an evolving hypothesis (noisy tenant + autoscaler threshold interaction + kernel fallback), immediate mitigations we ran during oncall, and a proposed lightweight runbook to catch the pattern earlier. Still draft — needs SRE + serving-runtime validation.

Why this matters:
- Dedicated customers expect predictable p95/p99. Gradual drift degrades SLAs and increases token cost (retries/timeouts).
- This incident showed an emergent class of failure where slow resource contention + autoscaler hysteresis produced repeatable bursts.

High-level timeline (UTC):
- 2025-02-08 04:10: first subtle p95 uptick observed on pool-gamma (0.2s -> 0.5s) in perf dashboards
- 2025-02-08 09:30: alert threshold for pool p95 crossed; auto-ticket created (JIRA-ENG-3487)
- 2025-02-09 01:00: on-call scaled pool manually (add 2 nodes) to reduce steady latency; limited improvement
- 2025-02-09 06:15: latency partially recovered but repeated micro-spikes began (~5–10m every hour)
- 2025-02-09 14:40: heavy noisy tenant (customer X, internal tenant id T-1024) observed high short-lived variance in GPU memory alloc + KV cache churn during spikes
- 2025-02-09 16:05: rolled a temporary routing policy to evict T-1024 to a quarantine pool; spikes subsided within 30m
- 2025-02-10 02:00: incident declared stable; follow-up work started

Detection signals we used (queries / commands):
- kusto: sum(p95_latency) by pool, bin(5m) -> trending
- temporary Grafana panel: top-10 tenants by device-mem-in-use (5m)
- serving runtime trace: kv-cache-hit-rate, kv-cache-size-by-tenant
- kube metrics: pod restart, OOM-kill counts (none observed), container_cpu_user_seconds_total

Quick hypothesis (ordered):
1) Noise tenant performing intermittent large-batch generation that increased KV cache and temporary memory pressure -> increased kernel fallback/serialization (FP16->FP32) for some ops -> per-token exec time increases.
2) Cluster autoscaler configured with conservative downscale/ upscale hysteresis so it reacted slowly; when it did add capacity it caused rebalancing, which temporarily magnified KV cache misses and triggered bursts.
3) A scheduling affinity rule allowed the noisy tenant to pack with latency-sensitive tenants (co-location), amplifying the externality.

Evidence for hypothesis:
- During spikes, per-tenant KV cache size for T-1024 went up 6x relative to baseline and then rapidly dropped after eviction.
- Kernel perf logs show switching to a safer execution path (~30% slower) on a subset of ops when free VRAM dropped below thresholds.
- Autoscaler logs show a single small-scale add event every ~4 hours (slow reaction), and eviction/rebalancing coinciding with spike windows.

Immediate mitigations applied (play-by-play):
- 2025-02-09 07:00: increased alert sensitivity to p95 slope (5m window) to detect re-emergence faster
- 2025-02-09 12:20: temporarily bumped pool target size by +2 nodes and disabled scale-down hysteresis (manual override) to observe behavior
- 2025-02-09 16:05: moved T-1024 to quarantine pool with taints+tolerations; observed p95 drop from 0.9s -> 0.32s in 30m
- 2025-02-09 18:10: reconfigured batch-scheduling policy to avoid packing high-memory tenants with low-latency tenants (short-term scheduler tweak)

Runbook draft: detection -> triage -> mitigation (short version)
1) Detection
   - Alert: p95(pool) > 2x baseline for 30m OR p95 derivative > 0.5s per 15m -> paging SRE
   - Query: top tenants by ephemeral-vram-alloc (5m), kv-cache-size-by-tenant (5m), pod_cpu and pod_gpu_mem metrics
2) Quick triage
   - Check quarantine pool load and last 6 hours of autoscaler events (kubectl logs autoscaler-controller)
   - Run: curl -s $RUNTIME/tracing/top-tenants?pool=POOLNAME | jq . | head
   - If a single tenant accounts for >30% peak KV-cache usage and increases temporally with spikes, consider quarantine move
3) Mitigation options (priority order)
   - Soft: increase pool capacity by +1 and disable scale-down for 1 hour
   - Medium: apply taint to noisy tenant nodes and migrate tenant
   - Hard: route noisy tenant to dedicated quarantine pool (billing/owner notification required)
4) Post-mitigation checks
   - Validate p95/p99 over next 2 hours, ensure no regression in other pools

Commands & quick snippets (notes to oncall):
- List top tenants by VRAM (internal tool): ssh infra-runner "/opt/infra/bin/top_vram --pool pool-gamma --window 5m"
- Temporary quarantine: kubectl label node <node> quarantine=true && annotate tenant T-1024 quarantine:true
- Autoscaler: kubectl edit cm gpu-autoscaler-config -n infra -> set scaleDownHysteresis: 2m (temp)
- Fetch kernel fallback logs: gcs://redwood-telemetry/kernel-switch/pool-gamma/2025-02-09/*.log.gz

Open action items (owners + ETA):
- infra/serving-runtime: instrument explicit kernel-fallback metric exposed to Prometheus (owner: Sofia Chen) - ETA 2025-02-28
- infra/autoscaler: add a "burst-detection" mode that temporarily lowers hysteresis when p95 slope detected (owner: Lewis Park) - ETA 2025-03-14
- sched: enforce soft anti-affinity label for customers with >X KB KV-cache (owner: Ava Martinez) - ETA 2025-03-07
- customer-success: notify customer X about observed noisy behavior and propose quota/plan changes (owner: Priya Shah) - ETA 2025-02-20

Longer-term ideas (brainstorm):
- Per-tenant adaptive KV cache quotas that throttle cache growth before it triggers kernel fallback
- Kernel path resilient thresholds (graceful degrade to avoid 30% slowdown spikes)
- Autoscaler integration with runtime signals (KV cache pressure as a first-class input)

Notes / things we weren't sure about:
- Unknown: whether some model variants trigger fallback earlier due to operator code paths; need model-onboarding team to audit T-1024 model ops
- We saw no OOMs but VRAM fragmentation could mimic effective pressure; need more fragmentation metrics

Postmortem status: follow-ups in progress. This doc is intentionally informal (working notes) — will convert to formal postmortem if follow-ups confirm hypothesis.

Appendix: quick links
- Incident ticket: JIRA-ENG-3487
- Quarantine runbook PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/892
- Dashboard snapshot: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/abcd/pool-gamma-latency

Notes-to-self:
- capture a 1h trace immediately after quarantine migration next time (high-sampling).
- add a Grafana alert for kernel-fallback rate (synthetic if metric missing).

End of draft.
